title: How Product Placement Works
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss product placement in film, TV, music, books and reality TV. They open with a teaser for the Science Channel's Pumpkin Chucking and touch on TiVo and DVRs skipping commercials. They cover the three ways placement happens (organic, trade for product, paid), and historical examples: the African Queen and Gordon's gin, E.T. and Reese's Pieces, Repo Man's generic products and tree air fresheners, The Firm and Red Stripe, Jerry Maguire and the Reebok deal, car placements (RoboCop's Ford Taurus, Audi R8 in I, Robot, Castaway's Wilson volleyball), American Idol sponsorship spending, Top Chef, Wayne's World, Stay Out of Maine-style subplot references, Fay Weldon's Bulgari Connection, branded kids' counting books, and Janis Joplin and Southern Comfort. The episode closes with a listener mail story about a speeding Corvette driver in Kansas.

segments.title: Opening banter and TiVo
segments.summary: Hosts plug the Science Channel's Pumpkin Chucking and The Road to Pumpkin Chucking, then discuss TiVo shipping its first product and DVRs letting viewers skip commercials, including how Nielsen factors DVR viewing into ratings.

segments.title: What product placement is and the three ways it happens
segments.summary: Introduces product placement and why it is harder in audio than visual media. Describes three routes: organic placement without company involvement, trade of free product for placement, and paid placement.

segments.title: Early examples: Sopranos Raid, E.T. and The African Queen
segments.summary: Discusses an unauthorized Raid can in The Sopranos, the Reese's Pieces payoff in E.T., and The African Queen's Gordon's gin, described as the first known product placement in a film. Notes soap operas' link to product placement.

segments.title: Repo Man, The Firm and Red Stripe
segments.summary: Covers Repo Man's generic products from Ralph's grocery and the air fresheners sent as free trees, then The Firm and the Red Stripe beer sales boost.

segments.title: Jerry Maguire and the Reebok lawsuit
segments.summary: Describes the Reebok deal in Jerry Maguire, the planned fake Reebok commercial at the end of the film that was cut, and the resulting lawsuit and settlement.

segments.title: Car placement in film and TV
segments.summary: Discusses cars in movies and TV: chase-scene emblems, The Transporter and Audi, Transformers and Camaro, RoboCop's Ford Taurus, Bond cars, Magnum P.I.'s Ferrari, Dukes of Hazzard, and Starsky and Hutch.

segments.title: I, Robot Audi, Cast Away and other examples
segments.summary: Covers the Audi RSQ concept car built for I, Robot, Cast Away's FedEx and Wilson volleyball, Risky Business Ray-Bans, and Tom Cruise's film appearances.

segments.title: Corporate placement business, American Idol and reality TV
segments.summary: Describes companies that employ staff for placement and spending figures for 2006, with most TV money going to American Idol. Discusses sponsor deals and reality shows like Top Chef that credit sponsors.

segments.title: Tongue-in-cheek placement, books, Janis Joplin and Southern Comfort
segments.summary: Covers Wayne's World and Josie and the Pussycats spoofs, a State and Main subplot, Fay Weldon's Bulgari Connection, branded children's books, the cheapest oldest placement in Take Me Out to the Ball Game, the upcoming Family Guy Windows 7 episode, and the Janis Joplin and Southern Comfort rumor.

segments.title: Listener mail: Kansas speeding Corvette
segments.summary: A listener named Jamie tells about his uncle Matt, who was pulled over in Kansas in the early 1980s in his Corvette and let off by a cop more interested in the car than a ticket.

segments.title: Grab bag and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts announce a grab bag segment for the week, invite listener email, and close the show.
